kurz: Without its backbone the chicken lies flat: it cooks faster and more evenly, and all of the skin faces up.
bild_im_kopf: Like a map spread out on the table: laid flat, everything is in view at once.
was_passiert: A whole chicken is round and uneven in thickness. Laid flat, breast and legs are a similar distance from the heat. The legs cook through before the breast dries out.
warum_wichtig: Cooking time drops considerably, by roughly a third (as a guide), and the skin crisps all over.
faustregeln: Keep the backbone: it makes a good stock.
schritte: Lay the chicken breast side down.
With poultry shears, cut along both sides of the backbone and remove it.
Turn it over and press firmly on the breastbone with the heel of your hand until it lies flat.
Pat the skin dry, salt and roast on a tray.
